column1: # NLRP1 inflammasome sensor across vertebrates — a true ortholog set whose
# members differ in domain architecture.
# Every row shares the same core, in the same order: NACHT nucleotide-binding
# domain, winged helix, HD2 helical domain, then FIIND / UPA-FIIND / CARD at the
# C terminus. What varies is the N terminus: a PYD (pyrin) death-fold domain is
# present in primates, dog and hedgehog and absent in rodents, artiodactyls,
# horse and fish. Rodent Nlrp1 lacking the PYD that human NLRP1 carries is the
# well-documented case (mouse Nlrp1a/b); the wider pattern here is as annotated
# by Pfam, and some rows are unreviewed entries whose gene models may under-call
# domains (cow has no LRRs called at all).
# The point for the viewer: in ungapped residue coordinates the shared NACHT sits
# at ~aa 328 in human and ~aa 134 in mouse, so a residue-anchored domain cartoon
# renders these orthologs as if their architectures disagreed. Column-locked,
# they stack — and the gap under the human PYD is where the missing module is.
# Human first so relativeTo="Human" is available, though the domain overlay,
# not the identity diff, is the story here.
# Tree caveat: ClustalW neighbor-joining recovers the primate, rodent and
# artiodactyl groupings, but pulls zebrafish (branch length 0.57, by far the
# longest) in beside the rodents rather than out as the outgroup — ordinary
# long-branch attraction. The tree is illustrative, as for every dataset here;
# the domain overlay is what this example is demonstrating.
